chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), he said:

I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! A man from your followers — news reached him that a man is giving away a sword and a horse in the way of God. So he went to him and took them both, while being ignorant of the proper manner of the Way (of Jihad). Then his companions met him and informed him that the Way with these (rulers) is not permissible, and ordered him to return them both.' So he (the Imam) said: 'Then let him do so.'

He said: 'He sought the man but did not find him, and he was told that the man had already departed.' He (the Imam) said: 'Then let him be stationed and not fight.' He said: 'In places like Qazween, al-Daylam, and Asqalan, and what resembles these border regions?' He (the Imam) said: 'Yes.' Then he said to him: 'Can he wage jihad?' He (the Imam) said: 'No, except if he fears for the offspring of the Muslims.'

He said: 'What do you think — if the Romans were to invade the Muslims, would it not be fitting for him to prevent them?' He (the Imam) said: 'He should be stationed and not fight. But if he fears for the very core of Islam and the Muslims, he may fight — and his fighting will be for himself, not for the (unjust) ruler.'

He said: 'I said: And if the enemy comes to the very place where he is stationed, how should he act?' He (the Imam) said: 'He should fight in defense of the core of Islam — not for these (rulers) — because in the extinction of Islam is the extinction of the religion of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.السلطان: The sultan/ruler — referring here to the illegitimate Abbasid caliph
key_terms.بيضة الإسلام: The egg/essence of Islam — a classical Arabic idiom for the vital core and integrity of the Islamic community
key_terms.ذراري المسلمين: The offspring/descendants of the Muslims — civilian Muslim populations
key_terms.سبيل الله: The way of God — here referring specifically to armed jihad
key_terms.مرابطة: Ribat — stationing oneself at a frontier post; a permitted form of border defense

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to wage jihad under an unjust ruler according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) addresses a follower's question about a man who took weapons donated for jihad but then learned that fighting under the current (Abbasid) rulers is not religiously sanctioned. The Imam's rulings reveal a core Shia political theology: participation in jihad under unjust rulers is prohibited, but defensive action to protect the very existence of Islam and Muslim communities is permitted — and when permitted, it is for God's sake, not the ruler's. This nuanced position was articulated during the Abbasid caliphate, when Shia Muslims faced the dilemma of military service under rulers they did not recognize as legitimate.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! A man from the ones in your<sup>asws</sup> Wilayah, news reached him that a man is giving away the sword and the horse in the Way of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. So he went over to him and took these two from him, and he was ignorant of the aspects of the Way (Jihad). Then he met his companion who informed him that the Way (Jihad) with them is not allowed, and instructed him with returning these two’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So let him do it’.

He said, ‘He sought the man, but did not find him, and it was said to him, ‘The man has left’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So let him be stationed (somewhere) and he should not fight’. He said, ‘So in (places) similar to Qazween, and Al-Daylam, and Asqalaan, and what resembles these border areas’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’. So he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Can he fight?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, except if there is a fear upon the Muslim offsprings’.

So he said, ‘What is your<sup>asws</sup> view, if the Romans were to enter upon (attack) the Muslims, would it not be befitting for him to prevent them?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should be stationed there and he should not fight. And if he were to fear upon the assets of Al-Islam and the Muslims, he can fight, so his fighting would happen to be for himself, and it would not be for the ruling authorities (i.e., a king or a caliph)’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘Supposing if the enemies were to come over to the place in which he was stationed, how should he react?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should fight about the eggs (assets) of Al-Islam, not about them, because in the extinction of Al-Islam is the extinction of the Religion of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim and Muhammad ibn ‘Isa have narrated from Yunus who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, one of followers had heard that a man gives away sword and horse for the cause of Allah. He went to that man and took the two items but he did not know the rules. His companions met him and told him that working in the way (of Allah) with these people is not permissible and they commanded them to return the items.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He should do so.’

The man said, ‘He searched for the man but did not find him. It was said that the man has left.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He should serve as a guard but he must not fight.’ The man then asked, ‘Should he serve as a guard in Qazwin, al-Daylam and ‘Asqalan?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, unless there is fear for the (offspring of) other Muslims.’

The man then asked, ‘Do you say that if Romans entered the lands of the Muslims, they should not stop them?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is to be on their guard but not fighting. However, if the center of al-Islam and Muslims is feared for, then one must fight. In such case his fighting is for his own sake and not for the authority (the king).’

The narrator has said that he then asked, ‘If the enemy comes to the place where he serves as a guard then what should he do?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He fights for the center of al-Islam but not for these people. It is because in the wear and tear of al- Islam is wear and tear of the religion of Muhammad, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause.’”
Ali has narrated from his father from Yahya ibn abu ‘Imran from Yunus from al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, a similar Hadith.
